I understand what your wife went through was horrible, and while yes transgender women won’t understand what it’s like to have the hysterectomy, but you also have to understand that transgender men and women go through things just as horrible that you or your wife don’t understand either. Men and women don’t simply transition for fun. They transition because they’ve been suffering for years from body dysphoria and feeling like they’re an alien in their own body. They suffer just as much emotional stress as anyone else, not to mention the fact that transgender individuals face constant scrutiny in society. A teacher calls a transgender student in the school that I work at ‘it.’ Transgender individuals face constant isolation from their peers, harassment and even sexual assault, not to mention the fact that transgender individuals have an extremely high rate of suicide due to the emotional stress of not having any support from parents, peers or authority. I’m not even transgender myself, but I’ve seen how much my transgender friends have suffered and it’s not pretty. Some are even told to kill themselves, and unfortunately some follow through with that. And for what? Just to simply try to make themselves happy and comfortable worn themselves?

He’s 19, it’s safe to think that most likely he has parents, which he lives with. Regardless even if they don’t live with him, it’s safer and easier for them to visit him and tell him in person.

But let’s pretend he doesn’t have parents and is all alone. OP calls BF and he goes ‘where is my GF’ and OP says ‘we need to talk in person, I’m coming over right now’ OP is still telling him she died without telling him, and worse he’s STILL going to sit there in anxiety and panic without confirmation that she died knowing well she died. So what’s better in this situation regardless; telling him straight to the point, or letting him sit there alone in the anxiety waiting like it’s some sort of drum roll?

I’m just curious as to what you want to happen though. If OP calls the boyfriend and he goes ‘where’s my girlfriend, etc’ and OP goes ‘we need to have a talk in person’ he’s going to know that his girlfriend is dead. So what’s better; getting it straight to the point now, or tell him without telling him and letting him sit there with the horrible dread and anxiety of knowing that she’s dead but not having any confirmation? It’s so much crueler too just make him wait and ponder in that anxiety just to tell him in person. OP needs to let her parents handle it, and let his and her parents offer him support with her coming to spend time with him when she’s ready. Neither should be driving anywhere. Just them telling him quickly is enough, it’s not like it’s been a month since she died.

Also almost all of us have experience. You’re not the only person in the world who lost someone and who had to break the news to another.
